Here goes something! I can feel the confidence increasing as I keep making great calls on price action with what I have learned here What better way than to share them in an online journal where like-minded folks can see and comment.

Many thanks, RTM for making this site possible. I truly believe I have found home!

For a trading plan, here is one slightly modified to trade harmonic patterns, and will adjust where needed as learning progresses.

Desired TF's: H4, H1, 30, 15. While paying attention to higher TF S/D areas and LTF decision areas. RVR - 2:1 - 4:1 Max loss on any trade 59 pips Max loss P/day 3% Lot size micro: max 0.3 no higher until 59 successful trades called / logged. Weekend rule: trades must be +75 to hold otherwise closed. Entry rules: Distinguished PA as taught by RTM must be present. Clear S/D, DP's, & S/R areas taken into account in each set up. I am finding I like to look for trades around poles and flag limits, FTR's and FTB's. Trade mgmt: First rule - always accept risk as a loss before taking any trade. Second Rule - set break-even at earliest convenience. Third rule - TP targets. With my harmonic trade plan, first tp was at 2:1 (prz to B point). Here, I will try to target obvious DP's that line up with rvr, and get a feel for what works and will adjust accordingly. I will also gladly accept any guidance from anyone who offers it.

Looking forward to the journey!

For a start, I had been browsing over at trading view, which is a great place to create online charts, and up pops a notice that I should go long on the USDCAD - that a great "buy" was setting up. I immediately wanted to go take a look and see for myself. So I put on my RTM glasses and lo and behold I saw something totally different. Now perhaps the fella was seeing something more longer term, but what I saw was a great possible short setting up.

Here is a screen cap of the set up as it was happening: Note this is not make anyone look bad. But to me, it seems rather revealing of some of the stuff being taught out there I suppose.

I jumped into the 4 hour and placed an ellipse in the area where price was at, and then added an arrow down. I saw the engulfs and to me it seemed as though price wanted to go back to the origin of the 4hr supply area.

تایم‌فریم‌های موردنظر: H4، H1، 30، 15. با توجه به نواحی S/D تایم‌فریم بالاتر و نواحی تصمیم‌گیری تایم‌فریم پایین‌تر. RVR - 2:1 - 4:1 ضرر حداکثر در هر معامله 59 پیپ، ضرر حداکثر در روز 3%. اندازهٔ لات میکرو: حداکثر 0.3 و تا وقتی 59 معاملهٔ موفق ثبت نشده بالاتر نرود. قانون آخر هفته: معاملات باید +75 باشند تا نگه داشته شوند وگرنه بسته می‌شوند. قوانین ورود: PA متمایز همان‌طور که RTM آموزش داده باید حضور داشته باشد. نواحی S/D، DP و S/R مشخص در هر ستاپ در نظر گرفته شوند. متوجه شدم که دوست دارم معامله‌ها را حول دکل‌ها و لیمیت‌های فلگ، FTR و FTB پیدا کنم. مدیریت معامله: قانون اول — همیشه ریسک را پیش از ورود به هر معامله به‌عنوان ضرر بپذیرید. قانون دوم — در اولین فرصت سر به سر کنید. قانون سوم — تارگت‌های TP. با برنامهٔ معاملاتی هارمونیک من، اولین TP در 2:1 بود (PRZ تا نقطهٔ B). اینجا سعی می‌کنم DP‌های واضحی را هدف بگیرم که با RVR هم‌راستا هستند، حس بگیرم چه چیزی جواب می‌دهد و بر همین اساس تنظیم کنم. همچنین از هرکس که راهنمایی ارائه دهد با کمال میل می‌پذیرم.

منتظر ادامهٔ این مسیر هستم!

I think these type of set ups can be traded time and again with amazing accuracy.

Here is a little set of management rules that can be used in doing so:

1. If you see an approach to a daily FTR. 2. Mark off any clear compression zone as price approaches the FTR. 3. Locate all fresh, non tested FTR'S on lower time frame (5 min 1 min). Look for big RN's near area. 4. If you have two FTR's on the lower time frame in close proximity of the RN, place entry at RN and stop above no more than two FTR's. PIP risk could be 10-20 pips max or whatever % your account will allow. 5 Target other side of CP zone.

I have embarked on primarily focusing on the last FTR's into the highest/lowest points of price structures (ie - QM's usually). Finding the origin of an engulf of these areas are often great places to TT with very little risk. For example, many of these from the 1 minute time frame can offer many times the reward of your risk. Testing in FXT2 with about 8 pips of risk as the max has been eye-opening.

Now think about that! Risking 8 pips, you could lose 7 out of 10 trades and still make money with a reward of 15.1. Actually, you could still make money with a 90% losing streak on 10 trades where you only won one trade with this kind of RR.

I don't think it has ever been more clearer to me than what I saw in this particular area of price on the GU. How interesting this is becoming.

The seeming logical progression 1. Price gives a clue it wants to go higher by engulfing into a CP PAZ above its flag. 2. Price engulfs out of flag indicating it wants to also go lower. 3. The second engulf point seems pivotal in that it creates a key leg that has the RBR that is used to hold price up to create the FL that is used to create the "High and Low"

of our QM. 4. Price after retesting FL, moves on to create our higher High that contains two very important FL's - the one becoming the point or origin where price will offer up the completion of the QM. 5. Once the FL is engulfed, the RBR is then used one last time to allow price to come & create the lower low of the QM.

فکر نمی‌کنم تا حالا چیزی برایم از آنچه در این ناحیهٔ خاص قیمت روی GU دیدم شفاف‌تر بوده باشد. این دارد جالب‌تر و جالب‌تر می‌شود.

پیشرفت به‌ظاهر منطقی: 1. قیمت با اینگالف به یک CP PAZ بالای فلگش سرنخی می‌دهد که می‌خواهد بالاتر برود. 2. قیمت با اینگالف از فلگ بیرون می‌آید که نشان می‌دهد می‌خواهد پایین‌تر هم برود. 3. نقطهٔ دوم اینگالف محوری به نظر می‌رسد چون یک پای کلیدی می‌سازد که RBR را دارد که برای نگه داشتن قیمت بالا استفاده می‌شود تا FL را بسازد که برای ساخت «بالاترین و پایین‌ترین»

QM ما استفاده می‌شود. 4. قیمت بعد از ریتست FL حرکت می‌کند تا بالاترین بالای ما را بسازد که دو FL بسیار مهم دارد - یکی نقطه یا مبدأی می‌شود که قیمت در آن تکمیل QM را ارائه می‌دهد. 5. وقتی FL اینگالف شد، RBR یک بار آخر برای اینکه قیمت برگردد و پایین‌ترین پایین QM را بسازد استفاده می‌شود.

Some sweet PA just prior to Crude oil inventories this morning. My goal is to get so good that I can see this as it is happening. This, to me, is the real skill! Forward Sight Reading <<< we want this

1. An area of some last demand below near the top of what appears to be a cp paz, (which seem to of had a nice clear engulf).

2. Price comes off a local higher high and FTR's & stalls before dropping into it. 3. Price performs a quick engulf back up and then drops to demand. I mark that structure and look for price to hold. Sure enough it does, price then surges nicely not too long after - engulfing the FTR back up, 4. Price rises to new highs - engulfing a very nice level above - then falls back and swaps nicely with recently engulfed FTR (which is also swapping with the last FTR into the local higher high, by the way) 5. From this point some small clues are given, price RT's back and offers a HH (green rectangle). Price then RT's back and offers a HL (yellow rectangle) 6. We are now 30 minutes away from the inventories release. And it wasn't surprising to see price momo past our chop box / fake highs and into an area that held price up before reversal to new lows. (i.e. the key FL / origin of move down, MPL, or whatever you like to call it)

Lastly, it was not at all surprising to see price surge down once it got below our demand area. Thanks for reading

(یعنی FL کلیدی / مبدأ حرکت به پایین، MPL، یا هر چی دوست داری صدایش کنی)

در آخر، اصلاً تعجبی نداشت که وقتی قیمت زیر ناحیهٔ تقاضای ما رفت، به پایین جهش کرد. ممنون از خواندن
